previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis due to sphincter of Oddi dysfunction was admitted with abdominal pain and nausea. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control initially. Her lipase decreased from 150 to 106, and she showed clinical improvement. She transitioned to oral pain medication and tolerated a clear liquid diet, then low-fat solids. The GI team evaluated her and scheduled an outpatient ERCP for the following week, with arrangements made for a female ASL interpreter. She was discharged home in stable condition with a plan to continue her home medications and follow up with her GI specialist.

Impression: The scout film was normal. 
Previous sphincterotomy in the major papilla 
The bile duct was deeply cannulated with the balloon. 
Contrast was injected and there was brisk flow through the 
ducts. Contrast extended to the entire biliary tree. 
The CBD was 6 mm in diameter. 
No filling defects were identified in the CBD. Opacification of 
the gallbladder was incomplete. The left and right hepatic ducts 
and all intrahepatic branches were normal. 
The biliary tree was swept with a 9-12mm balloon starting at the 
bifurcation. 
No stones or sludge were removed. 
Using a 6 mm dilater the ampulla was dilated. Excellent bile and 
contrast drainage was seen endoscopically and fluoroscopically. 
After the side viewing endoscope was removed from the patient, 
an forward viewing upper endoscope was used to visualize the 
esophagus, stomach and proximal duodenum. There were no 
abnormalities identified that would explain the patient's 
symptoms. 
Otherwise normal ercp to third part of the duodenum
